findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides website
findings.body: The serializer deliberately hides `website` (along with bio, location, etc.) for trust-level-0 users viewed by anonymous visitors via the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism (`include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list, and its value is derived directly from `object.user_profile.website`, so anonymous visitors now receive `website_name` (the website's host, plus full path when it matches the instance domain) in the JSON for TL0 users even though `website` itself is withheld. This defeats the anti-spam purpose of restricting those fields. The existing spec 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' will not catch this because `website_name` isn't in its attribute list either. Fix by adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or checking `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` in its include guard) and extend the spec to cover it.

findings.title: include_website_name is dead code — missing '?' so AMS never calls it
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers decides whether to serialize an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark), as used everywhere else in this file (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, etc.). The added method is named `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always included in the payload — serialized as explicit null for users who have no website — instead of being omitted when `website` is blank. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (or, better, add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` as noted in the other finding, which also defines the include predicate).

findings.title: Websites Ruby's URI parser rejects (e.g. IDN/Unicode domains) disappear from the profile entirely
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any stored website that Ruby's ASCII-only URI parser cannot handle, such as non-ASCII/IDN domains. `website_name` then returns nil, and since the template renders the globe icon and link only inside `{{#if model.website_name}}`, the user's website stops being displayed on their profile at all. The previous client-side code (`website.split("/")[2]`) still displayed the domain for such URLs, so this is a regression for affected users. Consider falling back to the raw `website` string when URI parsing fails instead of returning nil.

findings.title: No test for the sibling-subdomain branch of website_name
findings.body: The most complex branch of `website_name` — the `elsif` that compares parent domains when website and instance hosts have equal label depth greater than 2 (e.g. show the full path for `www.example.com` on a `forum.example.com` instance, but only the host for `www.other.com`) — has no test coverage. The three added examples only exercise the equal-host case and the website-domain-is-parent case, so a regression in the parent-domain comparison would not be caught.
